gold.answer: The square root of 2 is irrational. Assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms; then p² = 2q², so p² is even and p is even, p = 2r; then 4r² = 2q², so q² = 2r² and q is even, contradicting that p/q was in lowest terms. Therefore √2 is not rational.

answer.question: Prove that the square root of 2 is not rational.
answer.answer: √2 is irrational. Assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms; then p² = 2q², so p² is even, hence p is even, p = 2r. Substituting gives 4r² = 2q², i.e. q² = 2r², so q is even too — contradicting lowest terms. Therefore √2 is not rational.
evidence: Theorem 43 (Hardy & Wright): √2 is irrational, proof by infinite descent / parity.
Rudin §1.1 motivates the reals via the non-existence of a rational √2.

citations.claim: If √2 = p/q in lowest terms then p² = 2q², so p is even (p = 2r), forcing q even — contradiction.
The parity argument concludes: no p/q in lowest terms can satisfy p² = 2q².
